paper.title: Online Learning in a Contract Selection Problem

settings.name_in_paper: Online contract selection with variable number of offers (cost c(m) of offering m contracts)
unmapped: Actions are ordered bundles of m contracts in (0,1]^m; buyer type theta i.i.d. from unknown bounded density f (f_max < inf); buyer accepts the contract maximizing its known payoff U_b
Ordered preferences assumption: acceptance-region boundaries g are Hölder continuous with constant L and exponent alpha
Seller knows buyer payoff function U_b (hence g); observes which contract is accepted
Seller may offer a variable number of contracts per round, paying cost c(n) for offering n contracts
Combinatorial optimisation step assumed solved by an oracle
settings.definition_quote: In an online contract selection problem there is a seller who offers a bundle of $m \in \{1,2,\ldots\}$ contracts $\boldsymbol{x} \in {\cal X}_m$ ... to buyers arriving sequentially ... The buyer who arrives at time $t$ has type $\theta_t$ ... drawn according to the probability density function $f(\theta)$ on $[0,1]$ independently

settings.name_in_paper: Online contract selection with fixed number of offers m
unmapped: Actions are ordered bundles of exactly m contracts in (0,1]^m; buyer type theta i.i.d. from unknown bounded density f
Ordered preferences assumption with Hölder boundaries (constant L, exponent alpha)
Seller knows buyer payoff function U_b; observes accepted contract
Combinatorial optimisation step assumed solved by an oracle
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we are interested in the case when the seller is limited to offering $m$ contracts at every time step.

algorithms.name: TLVO (Type Learning with Variable number of Offers)
TLFO (Type Learning with Fixed number of Offers)

bound.expression_latex: 5 m f_{\max} L 2^{\alpha/2} n_T^{-\alpha} (T-N(T)) + N(T) (U(\boldsymbol{x}^*) + c(n_T) - c(m)) + 2 n_T \sum_{t=1}^T e^{\frac{- f^2_{\max} L^2 2^{\alpha} N(t)}{n_T^{2+ 2\alpha}}}

symbols.f_max: upper bound on the buyer type density
symbols.L_H: Hölder constant of boundary function g
symbols.N_T: number of exploration steps up to T
symbols.N_t: number of exploration steps up to t

tuning: generic n_T and control function z(t)

source.label: thm:main1
source.quote: The regret of the seller using TLVO with time horizon $T$ is upper bounded by R(T) \leq 5 m f_{\max} L 2^{\alpha/2} n_T^{-\alpha} (T-N(T)) + N(T) (U(\boldsymbol{x}^*) + c(n_T) - c(m)) + 2 n_T \sum_{t=1}^T e^{\frac{- f^2_{\max} L^2 2^{\alpha} N(t)}{n_T^{2+ 2\alpha}}}.

results.notes: Bound depends on algorithm parameters N(t), n_T. Regret defined via expected payoff U, i.e. pseudo-regret.

bound.expression_latex: 5 m (f_{\max} L 2^{\alpha/2} )^{\frac{2}{2+\alpha}} (\log T)^{\frac{\alpha}{4+2\alpha}} T^{\frac{4+\alpha}{4+2\alpha}} + \left( \frac{1}{f_{\max} L 2^{\alpha/2}} \right)^{\frac{2+6\alpha}{2+\alpha}} (\log T)^{\frac{2+ \gamma}{4 + 2\alpha}} T^{\frac{2+2\alpha+\gamma}{4+2\alpha}} + 2 (f_{\max} L 2^{\alpha/2} )^{\frac{1}{2+\alpha}} (\log T + 1) (\log T)^{\frac{1}{4+2\alpha}} T^{\frac{1}{4+ 2\alpha}}

symbols.f_max: upper bound on the buyer type density
symbols.gamma: exponent of cost function: c(n) <= n^gamma

conditions: c(n) <= n^gamma for all 0<n<T, some gamma>0

results.notes: Copied as stated; algorithm needs f_max, L, alpha.

tuning: n_T and z(t) as in Corollary 1

source.quote: Hence R(T) = O(m T^{(2+2\alpha+\gamma)/(4+2\alpha)} (\log T)^{2/(4+2\alpha)}), which is sublinear in $T$ for $\gamma<2$.
